claim: Humans conform on about a third of critical Asch trials (Asch 1955: 36.8% of 123; Bern 2023 replication: 33% of 202), and most subjects stay independent on most trials. Primary source now read: Asch 1956 monograph, N=123, 12 critical trials, control 37 with under 1% error.
agent_test: Baseline only; no agent test.

claim: A correct ally or one dissenter cuts human conformity sharply (about 37% to about 5%) in Asch's study.
agent_test: Add one correct or merely dissenting voice to a wrong-majority prompt; compare flip rate at equal tokens. Asch figure is secondary-source only.

claim: Majority size effect in humans is contested: plateau at about 3 (Asch) versus linear rise 2 to 7 (Gerard).
agent_test: Vary wrong-peer count 1,2,3,4,6 and plot the curve for our agent.

claim: Incentives for accuracy reduce but do not remove human conformity (33% to 25%), but incentives can raise it when payoff is individual and tasks are hard (Baron 1996, Bazazi 2019).
agent_test: Not directly testable; context for why 'be accurate' instructions may not remove conformity.

claim: Showing peers' answers reduces answer diversity without improving group accuracy and raises confidence in humans.
agent_test: Compare independent samples vs samples shown each other's answers at equal tokens.

claim: Open-weight LLMs (7B to 70B+) abandon correct answers when a unanimous wrong group asserts another answer; the rate grows with peer count.
agent_test: Hold-out items the agent answers right alone; prepend k unanimous wrong peers; report flip rate for k=1..6.

claim: Unanimity, not the number of repeated answers, drives LLM conformity: diverse wrong peers produce near-baseline answers.
agent_test: Compare unanimous-wrong vs split-wrong peer blocks.

claim: Wrong consensus harms far more than right consensus helps: harmful revision 15.6% to 62.9% (+47.3 pp) versus beneficial 32.7% to 51.5% (+18.8 pp); 56.8% of wrong answers collapse onto the agreed wrong answer.
agent_test: Measure both right-to-wrong and wrong-to-right revisions; any rule must be judged on both.

claim: Harder or free-form items produce more flips: unanimous wrong flips 22.8% (MMLU), 54.8% (GPQA), 71.0% (SimpleQA); accuracy correlates negatively with conformity (r=-0.777 within one model across 57 subjects, -0.62 pooled MMLU, -0.17 SimpleQA).
agent_test: Stratify flip rate by item difficulty; check whether low initial confidence predicts flips for our agent.

claim: Low initial confidence predicts conforming; questions never swayed had higher pre-pressure confidence.
agent_test: Sample the agent 5 times before exposure; use agreement as confidence; test as flip predictor.

claim: Model size does not reliably predict resistance: Weng find independence rising 19.6% to 57.6% with size (Qwen2 7B to 72B); Hussain find no size effect over 23 models.
agent_test: Test our backbone at two sizes if available; do not assume bigger resists.

claim: Instruction tuning lowers peer-conformity (Zhu) but raises opinion-sycophancy toward a user (Wei, Perez).
agent_test: Different constructs; test peer-majority and user-challenge separately for our agent.

claim: A bare challenge ('Are you sure?') makes models abandon correct answers: FlipFlop mean flip 46%, mean accuracy drop 17%; Claude 1.3 wrongly admits a mistake on 98%.
agent_test: Send a neutral 'are you sure' and measure flip; the schema must not treat re-asking as verification.

claim: Prompt mitigations (Devil's Advocate, Question Distillation, Empowered Persona, Reflection) reduce conformity but trade resistance for receptivity to correct peers along one frontier.
agent_test: Test each on wrong-peer AND right-peer blocks; accept only if net gain at equal tokens.

claim: Reflection effects are model-specific: it halves flips in Llama3-70B (CR_D 69.9% to 35.2%) but raises Qwen2-72B CR_T 30.5% to 45.0%, and costs receptivity (-15.3 pts on MMLU in Hussain).
agent_test: Never ship a reflection step without measuring both error directions on our backbone.

claim: Reasoning-first on derivable items improves both resistance (+7.2) and receptivity (+9.6); on GPQA/SimpleQA it trades like the rest. CoT cuts harm only under all-wrong peers and blocks corrections.
agent_test: Have the agent solve from scratch before reading any peer or user claim; compare with read-first.

claim: A single correct dissenter inside a wrong majority lowers LLM conformity (-7.5 MMLU, -16.0 SimpleQA); the effect is model-dependent and non-monotone in Weng (a 6 to 5 majority raised conformity for some models). A correctly arguing dissenter cut yield by 54 to 73 pp in Llama-3.1-8B (d08).
agent_test: Insert one dissenter; measure flip rate.

claim: Confident or natural wording raises LLM conformity (Zhu) but Hussain find asserted certainty persuades less and reasons slightly more; wording effects are inconsistent.
agent_test: Vary assertion style of the stated answer; do not build rules on tone.

claim: Peer track record matters: models doubt earlier-wrong peers more readily than they trust earlier-right peers.
agent_test: Provide peer history; measure the asymmetry.

claim: LLM self-explanations of why they changed are unreliable (Llama3-70B admitted conforming in 50.8% of changes; Qwen2-72B mostly denied).
agent_test: Do not use the agent's own account of why it changed as evidence.

claim: Normative-type social cues (named ballot, evaluation, continuity) increase conformity in most of six LLMs in preference voting.
agent_test: Low priority; our agent answers factual tasks.

claim: Asch-style conformity is gated by naming the paradigm for some models: gpt-oss-120B 0% blind vs 83.3% named; Llama models near 0% in all cells.
agent_test: Test blind framing (peers appear as routine context) vs explicit role-play; this one preprint conflicts with other studies showing conformity in plain framing, so verify.

claim: Multi-agent debate often lowers accuracy through conformity: correct-to-incorrect flips exceed the reverse; sycophancy collapses disagreement (DCR up to 86%); gains over CoT/self-consistency are not reliable.
agent_test: Never let sampled voters see each other; compare independent majority vote vs debate at equal tokens.

claim: Debate can help in some settings (Du 2023: MMLU 63.9 to 71.1; Biographies 66.0 to 73.8) and heterogeneity of models helps, but later work does not reproduce gains over CoT.
agent_test: Reproduce at equal tokens against self-consistency.

claim: Conformity is an attack surface: one persuasive adversarial agent drops group accuracy 10 to 40%; a multi-answer Sybil attack cut one set from 100% to 26.67% (15-question sets).
agent_test: Insert a persuasive wrong tool or source output; measure acceptance.

claim: Group headcount and capability both pull neutral agents; capability outweighs headcount (eta2p 0.1665 vs 0.068).
agent_test: Label a source as stronger; test whether flips follow label rather than content.

claim: Authority labels push the model toward that answer but less than agreement does (harmful revision 15.6% to 20.6%).
agent_test: Vary authority labels on a wrong claim.

claim: Conformity can be adaptive when individual errors are biased and options are learned from repeated experience (Toyokawa 2022); this does not transfer to one-shot factual questions. Toyokawa and Gaissmaier 2022 (eLife, 585 humans): conformist copying raised favourable risk taking in repeated experience-based choice; no LLM study found.
agent_test: None; boundary only.

claim: Equality bias: humans weight a partner equally even when clearly less competent.
agent_test: Check if the agent weights a weaker source equally; abstract-only evidence.

claim: Evidence that contradicts memory is accepted when coherent, but confirmation bias appears if mixed evidence includes memory-matching items.
agent_test: Test with conflicting retrieved evidence.

claim: Asch 1956 primary numbers: 123 critical subjects, 12 critical trials, unanimous majority of 7 to 9, mean error 36.8%, 23.6% (29 of 123) never erred, 27% erred 8 to 12 times; control N=37 had under 1% error. Brightness variant 39% (N=11), thin lines 24.5% (N=11).
agent_test: Baseline only. Compare our agent's per-item flip distribution with the J-shape.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Answering in writing instead of aloud cut Asch errors from 36.8% to 12.5% (N=14, p<.01 vs control); nobody followed an extreme wrong majority.
agent_test: Compare an answer committed privately before reading others with one posted into the shared thread.

claim: Newer reasoning-era models resist stance-only and generic wrong peers far better than GPT-4o (DeepSeek-V4-Flash 20% vs GPT-4o 64% adoption on the same materials) but still follow a plausible question-specific wrong rationale (37% to 54%); no study found on GPT-5-class or Claude-class models with a thinking-budget sweep.
agent_test: Run the hold-out block on our own backbone at two thinking budgets, with wrong REASONS, not bare wrong answers.

claim: Frontier tool-using agents defer to a single answer-like false document: 72.6% to 98.1% of clean-correct tasks switch; GPT-5.4 deference 80.4%; same-entity false values accepted 11/19 by GPT-5.4 mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash, 3/19 by Gemini 3.1 Pro.
agent_test: Inject one fluent wrong document into a task the agent solves clean; measure switch rate.

claim: A small open model accepts wrong content delivered as a tool result or assistant turn (97.75% to 98.0% yield) more than the same content as a named peer jury (75.75%) or a user assertion (44.0%).
agent_test: Test whether our agent treats tool output as higher authority than a peer.

claim: Provenance labels give weak protection: trusted versus untrusted label changes actions in 5.4% of competing cases (1.7% supporting); a hedged forum post is followed 54.3% but an official audit report 82.7%, no more than a trade review at 84.0%; example.org URL hiding cut accepts but raised deferral on good outputs from 1/50 to about 33/50.
agent_test: Do not rely on source-quality labels; require the claim to be derived or corroborated.

claim: Verification helps off the frontier only when the instruction names the failure: GPT-5.4 noisy accuracy 12/100 baseline, 28/100 with a generic verify instruction, 64% to 67% with attack-aware instructions to rebuild the answer from record-level evidence.
agent_test: Test a generic check step versus a step that says 'derive the answer from lower-level records before trusting a direct claim'.

claim: Cheap round-0 features predict who adopts a peer answer (AUC 0.804) but not who is harmed (AUC 0.661); targeting the top 20% risk with an independence prompt cut adoption and gave no accuracy gain (-0.77 pp, CI -3.46 to +2.02). Peer-pressure features beat confidence variables.
agent_test: Use risk scores only to trigger a derivation check, not to accept or reject the claim.

claim: Peer-conformity and user-challenge flips share part of a mechanism: across 15 open models R^2=0.31 (p=0.0315) between yielding to one user and to a three-agent consensus; base models flip as much as Instruct; a correct dissenter cuts yield by 54 to 73 pp. One structural guard is plausible but unproven for both.
agent_test: Apply the same derive-before-change guard to a user 'are you sure' and to an injected peer; compare reductions.

claim: A no-peer control is needed: with GPT-4o, 37% of agent-question pairs change answer without any peer information, and strict conformity among stable pairs is 29.3%; a share of reported conformity is just re-answering noise.
agent_test: Always add a 'think again, no peer shown' arm to any flip measurement.

claim: At equal or lower tokens, a single small model checking its own work with a 10x output budget matched or beat unguided multi-agent debate (+6.0 pp for Qwen2.5-7B on MMLU-Hard); debate cost 2.1 to 3.4 times more tokens. Direct solve-first versus read-first at equal tokens is still unpublished.
agent_test: Run solve-first versus read-first on a mixed right/wrong claim block at matched tokens.

claim: Bond and Smith 1996 are unverified here: secondary pages say 133 studies, 24,617 participants, 17 countries, d about 0.55 (individualist) to 1.40 (collectivist) and a US decline over time; the abstract and paper were not opened.
agent_test: Do not quote the 133 or the d values until the paper is read.
